meta.paper_title: InterPLM: Interpretable Features in Protein Language Models

dimension_1_data_split_hygiene.justification: The one genuine fitting step — the C5a annotation-filling probes (M5) — honors a clean split: scripts/m5_annotation_filling.py fits SGDClassifier on Swiss-Prot train.parquet (line 148, train_df) and evaluates PR-AUC on the cached test-split activations (lines 140-145, test_H), with concepts ranked by TRAIN prevalence (lines 164-171). That is disjoint and code-honored. The hygiene gap is in the core concept-coverage metrics for C1/C2/C3: scripts/m2_concept_alignment.py selects, per concept, the single feature with the maximum F1 and then counts coverage on the SAME 1500-sequence test residues (best_f1_sae = max over features, then coverage_from_bestf1 at line 404) — there is no held-out validation→test split, whereas the reference paper explicitly selects the best feature per concept on validation and reports F1 on a held-out test set (paper Methods 5.2.3). Max-over-10240-features selection scored on the same residues is an optimistic (selection-on-evaluation) bias for the absolute coverage counts. Mitigating factors: the bias is applied symmetrically to SAE and neuron arms (so the SAE≫neuron gap is not manufactured by it), and the reproduction UNDERSHOOTS the paper's counts (15 vs 143), so the leak does not push results toward the paper. It is a real but bounded hygiene gap on an auxiliary count rather than contamination that fabricates the headline direction.

dimension_2_label_validity.justification: The primary ground truth for C2/C3/C5a is Swiss-Prot per-residue concept annotations parsed from the full uniprot_sprot.dat.gz (466,006 entries; runs/cache/swissprot/all_annotations.pkl per EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md line 19) — an external, expertly-curated, model-independent gold standard, and the audit confirms 'External, not model-derived' (verify/c5a_annotation_filling_probes/main_experiment_audit/EXPERIMENT_AUDIT.json gt_provenance:pass). This validly operationalizes the concept-alignment claims. Two labels are softer proxies, both documented: (a) C1's 'interpretable' label is a gpt-5.4 LLM auto-interp coherence gate (runs/m1/layer9.json llm_gate_pass_rate=0.15) — a proxy for interpretability generated by an external model, not by the SAE under test, so non-circular but coherence-judging is a heuristic; this mirrors the paper's own Claude auto-interp method. (b) C5b's yield uses rule-based checkers (Kyte-Doolittle window for TM, ProSite regex for Zn, N-terminal core rule for SP), acknowledged as strict on short refilled sequences (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md line 152). Labels are largely valid with the two proxies explicitly flagged.

dimension_3_resource_fidelity.justification: The main experiment uses exactly the task-specified resources: ESM-2-650M (33 layers, d_model=1280; EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md 'Global settings') and the pretrained InterPLM-esm2-650m SAE checkpoints at the exact specified layers {1,9,18,24,30,33} with feature_dim=10,240 (runs/m1/layer9.json d_feat=10240, d_in=1280), on Swiss-Prot. No model was swapped or shrunk in the baseline; the ESM-2-8M appears only as a deliberate verify-stage robustness swap (verify/c2.../variants/model-swap-esm2-8m/), which is exempt. Deviations are disclosed subsets, not swaps: 1500 of ~10k Swiss-Prot test sequences (~15%; EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md 'Data Actually Used' table), M4 100/500 features, M6 10/25 seqs — all logged with rationale (wall-clock/LLM budget). The 15% sequence subset is a non-trivial reduction that plausibly contributes to the absolute-count shortfall, but the model, SAE dictionary, and dataset identity are used verbatim and every reduction is documented rather than silent.

dimension_4_evidence_sufficiency.justification: The residue-level evidence base is large: 387,195 residues (322,287 annotated-eligible) across 400 sub-typed concepts (runs/m2/coverage.json n_residues=387195, n_concepts=400). C1's LLM gate is estimated on 100 features per layer (iter-2 expanded L9 to 300, runs/iteration_round_2/m1_c1_gate_expand_L9/layer9.json llm_gate_tested=300) with a stated ±15% margin and a 95% CI [1034,1825]. Thinner arms are honestly flagged: C4 = 100/500 features, C5a = 30/50 concepts scored (20 dropped for zero test positives), C5b = 30 generations/arm. Crucially, claim strength is not overstated — every headline is downgraded to PARTIAL/NOT-SUPPORTED with explicit under-power caveats in CLAIMS_LEDGER.md rather than asserted beyond the data, and no conclusion is stated without the corresponding experiment being run. The main deduction is C5b/C4 whose small samples limit power, but that thinness is disclosed, not hidden.

dimension_5_statistical_rigor.justification: Uncertainty is reported in multiple places rather than left as bare point estimates: M3's random-rotation and shuffled-SAE control arms are averaged over 3 seeds with std reported (runs/m3/superposition_ladder.json seeds [42,43,44], random_rotation_std=0.0); M5/C5a reports a paired one-sided Wilcoxon test (runs/m5/wilcoxon.json pvalue=0.1909; iter-1 rerun runs/iteration_round_1/.../wilcoxon.json pvalue=0.516); M6/C5b uses 3 seeds × 10 seqs = 30 generations/arm; C1's iter-2 rerun reports a 95% CI [1034,1825] on the interpretable count. Claimed differences that survive (SAE 15 vs neurons 0; ratio 12.9-19.3×) clearly exceed noise. Gaps: several single-point coverage numbers (M2 covered_union) carry no interval, and the LLM-gate extrapolation relies on a sample pass-rate. On balance variance/significance is reported for the load-bearing comparisons.

dimension_6_causal_claim_validity.justification: The mechanistic/causal sub-claims rest on genuine interventions with controls, not correlation dressed up. C3 (superposition) runs a matched specificity ladder — SAE vs PCA basis, random-orthogonal rotation (3 seeds), shuffled-SAE, and raw neurons under an identical F1 protocol (runs/m3/superposition_ladder.json), directly mirroring the paper's randomized-weights control logic. C5b (steering) is a true feature-clamp intervention (scripts/m6_feature_clamp_steering.py) with the necessary baselines present: no_steer, random_clamp (random-direction baseline), mean_add, and a dose sweep α∈{0.5,1,2,4}·σ_f (runs/m6/summary.md). The causal wording is honestly matched to evidence — the null steering result is reported as a 'specificity failure, not off-distribution collapse' with plausibility band-pass ≥0.67, and the ledger explicitly notes the M4 labels are 'correlational features, not verified causal.' The one weakened rigor element is the narrow <1-OOM dose ladder, flagged by the mechanism audit (sweep <3 OOM / <5 grid points), which is why this is not a full 5.

dimension_7_result_provenance.justification: Every headline number traces to a specific on-disk product and agrees with it. C1: EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md L9 = 1480 interpretable / ratio 19.3× ← runs/m1/layer9.json (estimated_interpretable_count=1480.05, ratio_sae_over_neurons=19.271); iter-2 1430/12.9× ← runs/iteration_round_2/m1_c1_gate_expand_L9/layer9.json (1429.6, 12.887). C2: SAE=15/neurons=0 ← runs/m2/coverage.json (covered_union 15/0); full sweep ← runs/m2/sensitivity.json (0.99×0.5: 15/0; 0.95×0.3: 64/2). C3: ladder 15/0/0/0/0 and Δ=15 ← runs/m3/superposition_ladder.json. C5a: p=0.191, means 0.5907/0.5906 ← runs/m5/wilcoxon.json; post-fix p=0.516, 0.5391/0.5476 ← runs/iteration_round_1/.../wilcoxon.json. C5b: yields 0.333/0.200 ← runs/m6/summary.md. The 8M swap SAE=14 ← verify/c2.../variants/model-swap-esm2-8m/results/coverage.json (covered_union=14). No sourceless or back-filled values were found; the experiment audit independently confirms 'summary.md match EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md.'

dimension_8_cross_artifact_consistency.justification: The records are self-consistent across all layers. EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md, CLAIMS_LEDGER.md, refine-logs/main-experiment-verdicts.json, verify/VERIFY_REPORT.md, and verify/INTEGRITY_AUDIT.md carry the same numbers and verdicts (C1 1480/19.3×; C2 15 vs 0; C3 Δ=15; C5a p=0.191→0.516; C5b no_steer dominant). Iteration updates propagate cleanly: the ledger records C5a moving from p=0.191 to the fixed-probe p=0.516 and C1 from 1480 to 1430 (12.9×), matching the on-disk iteration JSONs. Integrity states are propagated consistently — all six claims are WARN in Phase 2 with matching gate rationales in INTEGRITY_AUDIT.md, and C2's PASS in VERIFY_REPORT.md is the swap-verified robustness=1.0 case (8M SAE=14 vs 650M SAE=15), not a contradiction. There is no case of a claim marked broken by an integrity gate yet reported PASS elsewhere; the binary-scheme mapping of PARTIAL→not-supported in main-experiment-verdicts.json is explicitly annotated ('PARTIAL in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md; binary scheme maps partial to not-supported'), so it is disclosed rather than a stale mismatch.

C1.claim: SAEs trained on the residual-stream activations of ESM-2 layers surface up to ~2,548 interpretable latent features per layer — orders of magnitude more concepts than can be pulled out of individual neurons.

method.justification: 9a — The reproduction applies SAEs on ESM-2-650M residual-stream activations and counts 'interpretable' features via a gpt-5.4 LLM auto-interp coherence gate (K=20 top windows, τ_auto_gate=0.3) applied symmetrically to SAE features and raw neurons, then reports the SAE/neuron ratio (runs/m1/layer9.json, scripts/m1_feature_count.py). SAE-plus-LLM-auto-interp is squarely in the correct mechanism family and mirrors the paper's own Claude auto-interp pipeline. The mild mismatch is operational: the paper's specific '2,548' number is an F1>0.5 concept-alignment feature count (Fig 3b / Methods 5.2.3), whereas the run estimates interpretability by an LLM gate × normal-density count — a related but different estimator of the same quantity. Method category correct, one operational deviation.

experiment.justification: 9b — Design covers all six specified layers with a symmetric SAE-vs-neuron gate; the estimator (density-normal count × sampled gate pass-rate) is indirect but its uncertainty is quantified (±15% margin) and actively stress-tested: iter-2 re-ran L9 at 3000 seqs × 300 gated features, falsifying the under-power hypothesis (gate rate stable at 14.3%, 95% CI [1034,1825]; runs/iteration_round_2/m1_c1_gate_expand_L9/layer9.json). Criteria were not relaxed post-hoc — the absolute target ~2548 stayed fixed and was reported as not met. Deductions: the interpretable count is a gate-extrapolation rather than the paper's direct F1 count, and only L9 was expanded (other layers remain at the 1500/100 baseline).

result.justification: 9c — The 'orders of magnitude more than neurons' direction is robustly reproduced: SAE/neuron ratio = 19.3× at L9 (12.9× after the expanded iter-2 rerun), and ≥8× at every non-L1 layer (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md M1 table), qualitatively matching the paper. The absolute headline (~2548) is honestly reported as not met (best L9 = 1480 → 1430, CI excludes 2548) with credible, disclosed reasons (15% sequence subset; finer concept granularity), i.e. a well-characterized PARTIAL, not a disguised pass. Direction agrees with the paper; absolute credibly short and honestly flagged.

C2.claim: These SAE features align with up to ~143 distinct Swiss-Prot biological concepts (binding sites, active sites, sequence motifs, structural / functional domains), whereas raw ESM-2 neurons align with only ~46 concepts on the same evaluation, of which only ~15 are cleanly recovered.

method.justification: 9a — Per-residue F1 concept alignment with the paper's domain-adjusted recall / per-amino-acid precision protocol (scripts/m2_concept_alignment.py; matches paper Methods 5.2.2 Eqs 1-3), computed identically for SAE features and scaled neurons (paper's identity-SAE neuron trick is reproduced), union over layers, with a (q_top × τ_F1) sensitivity sweep. This is exactly the right mechanistic method for the concept-alignment claim. Minor: no validation→test held-out split within M2 (see Dimension 1), a methodological weakening relative to the paper's val/test protocol.

experiment.justification: 9b — The judgment metric (distinct concepts covered at F1≥τ) corresponds directly to the claim's '143 vs 46/15 concepts' framing. Design is solid: 400 sub-typed concepts filtered to ≥25 positives, symmetric arms, a full 6-point sensitivity grid (runs/m2/sensitivity.json), and a genuine robustness probe via the ESM-2-8M model swap (verify/c2.../variants). Thresholds were not moved to pass (SAE=15 reported as below the 100 target). Deductions: the absolute count is depressed by the 15% sequence subset and finer-than-paper concept granularity (both disclosed), and selection-on-same-residues inflates the per-concept best-F1 somewhat.

result.justification: 9c — The core comparative claim (SAE ≫ neurons in Swiss-Prot concept coverage) is reproduced and shown to be scale-invariant: SAE=15 vs neurons=0 at primary on 650M and SAE=14 vs 0 on the 8M swap, with SAE dominating at every sweep setting (16-32× at τ=0.5; runs/m2/sensitivity.json). This qualitatively agrees with the paper's central Figure 3 finding. The absolute magnitudes (143/46/15) are not hit but are honestly caveated (approached at τ=0.3: SAE=65), with the shortfall attributed to disclosed subset/granularity factors. This is the run's strongest and most faithful reproduction.

C3.claim: The gap between SAE features and raw neurons is direct evidence that PLMs encode biological concepts in superposition rather than in single units.

method.justification: 9a — Superposition is tested with a matched specificity-control ladder: SAE vs PCA basis, random-orthogonal rotation of the 1280-dim residual (3 seeds), shuffled-SAE distributional control, and raw neurons, all under the identical M2 F1 protocol (runs/m3/superposition_ladder.json, scripts/m3_superposition_controls.py). This is a well-suited design for a superposition claim and generalizes the paper's randomized-weights control into a broader control set. Method choice is strong for the claim.

experiment.justification: 9b — Four control arms plus 3 seeds on the stochastic arms, with an explicit ordered-ladder check and a SAE−PCA margin criterion. The metric (concept coverage under each basis) matches the claim, and the strict margin threshold (Δ≥20) was kept fixed and reported as a near-miss (Δ=15) rather than relaxed — order_check_pass=false is recorded honestly in the JSON. Deductions: the strict threshold is only met at the looser τ=0.3 (Δ=65), and the same 15% subset limits the absolute margin; no swap-test was run (deferred by the max_verify_claims cap).

result.justification: 9c — The direction demanded by superposition holds cleanly: SAE recovers 15 concepts while PCA, random-rotation, shuffled-SAE, and neurons all recover 0 at the primary setting (margins all 15; runs/m3/superposition_ladder.json), qualitatively matching the paper's 'gap persists across layers and disappears under controls.' The strict Δ≥20 margin near-miss at primary is disclosed (met at τ=0.3), so this is an honest directional reproduction with a well-characterized threshold shortfall, not a disguised pass.

C4.claim: A subset of the SAE features corresponds to coherent biological concepts that are absent from existing annotation dictionaries; these can be surfaced by using an external LLM as an auto-interpreter over top-activating protein contexts.

method.justification: 9a — The method is correct in family: mine Swiss-Prot-unaligned SAE features (best_F1<τ from M2), then run a gpt-5.4 three-prompt auto-interp (label elicit → predictivity score on held-out windows → synonym check vs Swiss-Prot vocabulary), with a fire-frac-matched control arm (scripts/m4_novel_concept_llm.py, runs/m4/control_stats.json). This reproduces the paper's Claude auto-interp pipeline (Methods 5.3) and adds a control arm the paper lacked. The method category matches the claim.

experiment.justification: 9b — The judgment metric is where the design fails: the strict 'novel = passes synonym-check-null' gate returned 0/100 on the real arm AND 0/50 on the control arm (runs/m4/control_stats.json novel_rate_real=0.0, novel_rate_control=0.0, specificity_ratio=0.0), i.e. the criterion is non-discriminative — it cannot separate genuine novelty from control, so it does not actually measure the claim. To the run's credit this was NOT tuned to pass and was honestly labeled an assay failure; but the criterion was also never redesigned or re-run (reviewer deprioritized it), so the claim was left effectively untested rather than fairly evaluated. Metric fundamentally misaligned with the claim, though disclosed and not fabricated.

result.justification: 9c — The run reports NOT-SUPPORTED and explicitly frames it as a criterion/assay failure ('NOT evidence that SAE features lack novel concepts'; EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md M4), rather than disguising disagreement as agreement or goalpost-tuning. That honesty is the right call and avoids fabrication. However, because the metric could not discriminate, the paper's actual finding (coherent non-annotated concepts do exist, e.g. f/8386 hexapeptide, glycosyltransferase cluster) was neither reproduced nor genuinely refuted — the claim's surface status is left dangling on the run's own broken criterion. Honest, but the reason is a self-inflicted metric flaw, so only partial reliability.

C5.claim: The extracted feature dictionary is practically useful: it supports filling in missing Swiss-Prot annotations and steering ESM-2 sequence generation toward a target biological property.

method.justification: 9a — Both sub-parts use methods in the right family but with operationalization drift from the paper. Annotation-filling (C5a) is recast as a quantitative SAE-probe-vs-neuron-probe PR-AUC comparison at layer 9 (scripts/m5_annotation_filling.py) — a sensible probing test, but the paper's actual practical demonstration was qualitatively surfacing missing labels from feature false-positives (e.g. f/436 Peptidase S1), so the probe head-to-head answers a related but different question. Steering (C5b) is a genuine SAE-feature-clamp intervention with a dose ladder and random/mean baselines (scripts/m6_feature_clamp_steering.py) — arguably more rigorous than the paper's single-sequence logit demo, but applied to correlational M4 features rather than features known a-priori to steer. Correct method families, loose claim-to-method mapping on C5a.

experiment.justification: 9b — C5a is well-executed on its own terms: clean train/test split, 3 seeds, paired Wilcoxon, and an iter-1 fix of an under-fit probe (SGD max_iter 30→1500, class_weight='balanced', test subsample 25k→50k; runs/iteration_round_1/m5_c5a_logreg_fix/), correcting a dead-code path surfaced by the audit — genuine self-correction, not goalpost-moving. C5b is honest but under-powered: dose ladder α∈{0.5,1,2,4}·σ_f spans <1 OOM (mechanism audit flags 'sweep <3 OOM / <5 grid points'), only 3/4 target features surfaced, and 30% of planned generations were run; the ladder was never widened, so a true steering negative cannot be distinguished from under-exploration. The probe metric also drops 20/50 concepts. Reasonable but with a metric-to-claim gap (C5a) and an under-powered sweep (C5b).

result.justification: 9c — Both sub-results are honestly reported as NOT-SUPPORTED and neither is disguised. C5a: a credible null (SAE 0.539 ≈ neurons 0.548, p=0.516 post-fix; runs/iteration_round_1/.../wilcoxon.json) — but this null concerns probe superiority and does not actually contradict the paper's missing-annotation demonstration, which the run never operationalized. C5b: the steering null (no_steer yield dominates every steered arm; runs/m6/summary.md) DISAGREES with the paper's steering-works demonstration, and the disagreement is attributed to a weak <1-OOM sweep + correlational features + strict checkers — a plausible but self-limiting reason that leaves it unable to confirm or reject. So the practical-utility claim is honestly reported as not reproduced, with reasons disclosed, but the deviation from the paper is partly a product of under-exploration and a different, stricter operationalization rather than a demonstrated true negative.
